title: GTA 6 Ultimate Edition Drives Strong Pre-Order Sales
description: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick reveals that many players pre-ordering Grand Theft Auto 6 are opting for the higher-priced Ultimate edition.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## GTA 6 Pre-Orders: Players Favoring the Higher-Priced Ultimate Edition

As anticipation for *Grand Theft Auto 6* continues to build across the gaming community, pricing and packaging strategies remain a major talking point. While many may baulk at the idea of paying triple-digit sums for a video game, recent insights from the top suggest that the market's appetite for premium content is stronger than expected.

### Strong Demand for Premium Tiers

According to Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Rockstar's parent company Take-Two, a significant portion of the people who have already pre-ordered *Grand Theft Auto 6* are bypassing the $80 (£70) Standard edition in favor of the more expensive Ultimate edition, bringing their purchase price up to around $100 (£90).

This trend highlights a fascinating consumer behavior within the modern gaming landscape. Despite initial resistance or debate surrounding rising game prices, the most dedicated fans are clearly willing to invest more to secure the most comprehensive version of what is widely considered the most anticipated entertainment release of the decade.

### Industry Implications

While general consumer sentiment can often lean toward caution regarding price hikes, mega-franchises like GTA operate under slightly different rules. The willingness of players to lean into the $100 price point for the Ultimate edition suggests that perceived value, brand loyalty, and the sheer scale of the anticipation can heavily outweigh initial sticker shock.

## Editor's Take
Take-Two's revelation about *GTA 6* pre-orders underscores the immense pulling power of Rockstar's franchise. When core fans are readily opening their wallets for the $100 tier, it signals a shifting acceptance of premium pricing for generational blockbusters, setting a potent benchmark for the rest of the AAA industry.
